definition: Mapping text across scripts (Arabic ↔ Latin) preserving pronunciation: proper names, Arabizi normalization, cross-lingual search.
details: Mapping text across scripts (Arabic ↔ Latin) preserving pronunciation: proper names, Arabizi normalization, cross-lingual search. Ambiguous in both directions (one Arabic name has many valid Latin spellings), so treated as a sequence modeling task, not a lookup table.

explainer.lead: Transliteration maps text across scripts, such as Arabic to Latin, while preserving pronunciation. It matters for proper names, Arabizi normalization and cross-lingual search.

tiers.eli5: It's writing a name in another alphabet so it sounds right, like spelling an Arabic name in English letters the way it is pronounced.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers treat transliteration as a sequence modeling task rather than a lookup table, because ambiguity runs both ways and one Arabic name has many valid Latin spellings.
tiers.paperLevel: Transliteration is a mapping between scripts that preserves pronunciation; because both directions are ambiguous, it is modeled as a sequence task rather than a deterministic table.

explainer.example: A single Arabic name may have several accepted Latin spellings, so a transliteration model must score candidates rather than return one fixed string.
